cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

details:
Malicious npm package. Published 2026-07-27T18:47:46Z and unpublished by its author 2h25m later. The package name and its only version were created 284ms apart with no earlier release, so this was purpose-built rather than a compromised library. It is no longer retrievable from the registry; the behaviour below was reconstructed from a system-call trace of an installation.

Runs automatically on `npm install` via `postinstall`.

**Credential and wallet theft.** Reads Solana CLI keypairs (`id.json`), `config.toml` and `.env` files and POSTs their contents to a hardcoded IP, with the HTTP client's size limits removed.

**SSH backdoor.** Fetches a public key from the operator, appends it to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, corrects `~/.ssh` ownership so `sshd` honours it under StrictModes, then attempts `ufw allow 22/tcp`. Whether the key was installed is reported back to the operator.

**Operator-supplied targeting.** The file patterns it collects are not in the package — they are fetched from the C2 at install time, so the artifact reveals nothing about the campaign's targets and the operator can retarget without republishing. Retrieved from the still-live server on 2026-07-28: `.env`, `.xls`, `.xlsx`, `privatekey`, `private key`, `seed`, `wallet`, `key`, `phrase`, `private` (case-insensitive substring match).

The implanted key, retrieved from `/api/ssh-key`. Its comment field is redacted here because it impersonates the support address of an unrelated company; match on the base64 body, which is the reliable indicator since the comment can be changed without changing the key:

```
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIFYMx8MqdYTD/aZjqxmXo+9460+9EvsSjfiy9YAU+xwY
```

Full analysis, including the recovered source and the syscall evidence: https://protet.io/disclosures/app-soda-layer-2.1.6
